1. THE GAP-FILLING RULE DOES NOT REACH THE CONTROLS IT NAMES — and this breaks the claim's own load-bearing sentence. field-mode.css asserts: "Controls that carry no inline shadow of their own — ghost buttons, nav items, rail tiles — get the edge from here. Anything with an inline box-shadow keeps it: inline wins, and it is already ringed by the tokens above." Both halves fail for ghost controls, because they DO carry an inline box-shadow — the literal string "none". Button.jsx: "ghost:     { bg: \"transparent\", color: \"var(--text-secondary)\", shadow: \"none\", hoverShadow: \"none\" }" applied as "visual = { background: hover ? \"var(--neutral-bg)\" : \"transparent\", color: v.color, boxShadow: \"none\" };". IconButton.jsx: "ghost: { bg: hover ? \"var(--neutral-bg)\" : \"transparent\", color: \"var(--text-secondary)\", shadow: \"none\" }". An inline box-shadow:none beats the un-!important "[data-field-mode=\"on\"] :is(button,[role=\"tab\"],[role=\"button\"]):not(:disabled){\n  box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 1.5px var(--field-edge);\n}". So the ghost button — transparent background, no fill, no shadow, --text-secondary text, the LOWEST-contrast control in the system and the first item in the rule's own list — gets no edge in field mode. It is neither ringed by tokens nor filled by the rule; the comment's reasoning has a third case it never considered. (Nav items and rail tiles genuinely do work: AppRail.jsx's RailButton and NavItem set no inline boxShadow at all.)

2. THE USER-FACING PROMISE IS FALSE. FieldModeToggle.jsx ships this default copy: hint = "Stronger text, visible edges on every card and control. For working in direct sunlight." "every card and control" is untrue per finding 1, and untrue for ListRow.jsx, which at rest is "background: hover ? \"var(--surface)\" : \"transparent\"" with "boxShadow: hover ? \"var(--e2)\" : \"none\"" — a div, so neither the token ring nor the :is(button…) rule touches it. The resting list row, the densest repeated surface on a phone, gains nothing; its only edge is hover-only, which a touch user never sees — and readme.md itself forbids that: "Nothing is hover-only, anywhere." readme.md's "every surface in the product already reads box-shadow: var(--e2) — which is where the borders come from" is the old-behaviour law left standing.

3. THE SPECIMEN OFFERED AS PROOF BREAKS WHEN YOU USE IT. field-mode.css defines only [data-field-mode="on"] — there is NO [data-field-mode="off"] rule anywhere. Custom properties inherit, so guidelines/field-mode.card.html's left pane, "<Stage mode=\"off\" title=\"Default\"/>" rendering "<div className=\"stage\" data-field-mode={mode}>", cannot un-inherit. The card ships its own "<FieldModeToggle/>" at the top, whose apply() does "document.documentElement.setAttribute(ATTR, on ? \"on\" : \"off\")" — flip it and <html> carries "on", the tokens cascade into BOTH panes, and the side-by-side comparison the card exists to make collapses into two identical field-mode panes. The claimer cited this card as proof both modes render side by side; they do, only until you touch its switch.

4. .d.ts / .jsx / consumed-component disagreement on a live prop. FieldModeToggle.d.ts declares "density?: \"expressive\" | \"functional\";" and FieldModeToggle.jsx defaults "density = \"expressive\"" then forwards it: "<Switch checked={on} onChange={(e) => setOn(e.target.checked)} label={label} density={density} />". Switch takes no such prop — Switch.jsx's signature has none and Switch.d.ts's SwitchProps is "checked / onChange / label / disabled / id / style". The prop is typed, documented, defaulted and silently discarded. Harmless at runtime, but it is a declared-but-dead API on the single component this gap delivers.

5. THE CAPABILITY REACHES ZERO SCREENS. templates/mobile-field-app/app.jsx — the phone-on-a-roof reference build, the exact user this mode exists for — destructures "{ AppRail, BottomNav, Fab, SearchField, ScopeToggle, FilterChips, SortPills, FiltersButton,\n    DataTable, RecordCard, NextAction, StatusChip, Avatar, LogoTile, Button }" and never references FieldModeToggle; its "More" tab is a stub. No template surfaces the switch, and _ds_manifest.json has "startingPoints":[] despite FieldModeToggle.d.ts's "@startingPoint section=\"Forms\"". A surveyor in the product has no way to turn it on.

On the disclosed selector deviation: I confirm readme.md still says "`tokens/field-mode.css` scopes `:root[data-field-mode=\"on\"]`" while the file uses the bare attribute. The claimer waves this off as cosmetic; it is not — the bare attribute is strictly broader, and that breadth combined with the missing "off" rule is precisely what causes finding 3. The doc is wrong and the deviation has a consequence its own comment did not anticipate.

Verdict: PARTIAL. Present: the token scope, correct import order and specificity, a working persisted global toggle with a matching Switch API, real token inheritance into inline-styled components, no per-component prop, both readme border-exception statements updated, a registered specimen, and a compiled manifest. Missing: the edge on ghost Button/IconButton and on resting ListRow (so "visible edges on every card and control" and readme's "every surface" are both false as shipped), a [data-field-mode="off"] reset that would make the subtree-scoping story actually work, agreement between FieldModeToggle's density prop and Switch, and any product surface that exposes the switch.
